title: Compute brief - 3 November 2026
description: Anthropic's amended S-1 puts its committed compute and infrastructure spend at about $895.4 billion, more than double the $417 billion it listed before. On the supply side, Crusoe has posted on-demand price rises from 1 December: H100 $3.90 to $4.50, H200 $4.29 to $5.40, B300 $8.96 to $9.90. Wire: Drax plans a GW-scale UK campus, Aramco closes 49% of HUMAIN, Russia orders a 10% state reserve in private data centres. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Demand is contracted. Supply is repricing.
lede: Anthropic amended its S-1 on 3 November with third-quarter revenue of $17 billion and a net loss of $23.29 billion, and its purchase commitments and leases now total about $895.4 billion, substantially all for compute and infrastructure, up from $417 billion previously listed. The filing names $121.3 billion with Google, $120.5 billion with SpaceX, $110 billion with Amazon, $44.9 billion with Microsoft, $44.6 billion with Nscale, $41.3 billion with Lambda and $50 billion with Fluidstack, per DCD. Against last week's neocloud credit squeeze, the supply side is starting to reprice: Crusoe's public price page now shows new on-demand rates from 1 December 2026, with H100 up 15.4% to $4.50, H200 up 25.9% to $5.40 and B300 up 10.5% to $9.90 per GPU-hour. Today's live prints are unchanged, so the tape shows 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW; Lambda H100 holds at $3.99 and B200 at $6.69.
